## What CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 requires

- **Attribution.** Credit the licensor, link this license, and indicate if
  changes were made. IMPPAT's homepage also asks anyone who uses the resource
  to cite the three articles listed in [README.md](README.md).
- **NonCommercial.** The legal code defines NonCommercial as use "not primarily
  intended for or directed towards commercial advantage or monetary
  compensation." That test looks at the purpose of the use. It does not turn
  on whether the user is a company. Detail is in the research-use section.
- **NoDerivatives.** The legal code allows you to produce and reproduce
  Adapted Material for NonCommercial purposes only, and it withholds the right
  to Share that Adapted Material. Share includes distribution and making
  material available to the public.
- **Sui generis database rights.** Section 2(b) of the legal code applies when
  those rights cover the database. Extraction and reuse of all or a
  substantial portion of the contents are limited to NonCommercial purposes,
  and a database that includes a substantial portion of the contents is
  Adapted Material. Derived registry rows and tables must not be committed or
  distributed.
- **No extra downstream restrictions** on the licensed material, and no
  suggestion that IMSc endorses Herbenzo.

Until IMSc grants written permission, keep IMPPAT files, subsets, and
derivatives out of git, out of releases, and out of the ingredient registry.

## Research use

**Not legal advice.**

CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 judges NonCommercial by purpose: a use that is not primarily
intended for or directed towards commercial advantage or monetary
compensation. Creative Commons' interpretation page states that this does not
depend on the user's identity — a for-profit organization can have a
non-commercial purpose, and a nonprofit can have a commercial one.
<https://wiki.creativecommons.org/wiki/NonCommercial_interpretation>

The owner has described the intended evaluation as research. Exploratory
research may qualify under that purpose test. Use that feeds Herbenzo product
development or SKU design is likely commercial, because that purpose is
directed toward commercial advantage.

NoDerivatives in the 4.0 legal code permits private adaptation (produce and
reproduce Adapted Material) and forbids Sharing Adapted Material. The same
license covers sui generis database rights, so derived registry rows and
tables must not be committed or distributed.

Conditions for a research evaluation:

- Give attribution and cite IMPPAT as the site requests (see [README.md](README.md)).
- Keep the purpose non-commercial.
- Do not redistribute the data or any derivative.
- Keep the data and any derivative out of product output and regulatory output.

Get written permission from IMSc (Areejit Samal, `asamal@imsc.res.in`) before
any product-facing use.
